chrome.notes: Saved passwords are encrypted by Windows (DPAPI) and cannot be decrypted after a reinstall: the user gets a different key on the new system. Bookmarks, extensions and history do carry over. Syncing passwords and bookmarks with your Google account is more reliable.

edge.notes: Saved passwords are encrypted by Windows (DPAPI) and cannot be decrypted after a reinstall: the user gets a different key on the new system. Bookmarks, extensions and history do carry over. Syncing passwords and bookmarks with your Microsoft account is more reliable.

brave.notes: Saved passwords are encrypted by Windows (DPAPI) and cannot be decrypted after a reinstall: the user gets a different key on the new system. Bookmarks, extensions and history do carry over. Syncing passwords and bookmarks with Brave Sync is more reliable.

vivaldi.notes: Saved passwords are encrypted by Windows (DPAPI) and cannot be decrypted after a reinstall: the user gets a different key on the new system. Bookmarks, extensions and history do carry over. Syncing passwords and bookmarks with your Vivaldi account is more reliable.

opera.notes: Saved passwords are encrypted by Windows (DPAPI) and cannot be decrypted after a reinstall: the user gets a different key on the new system. Bookmarks, extensions and history do carry over. Syncing passwords and bookmarks with your Opera account is more reliable.

yandex.notes: Saved passwords (Ya Passman Data) are protected by a key that Windows encrypts (DPAPI) and cannot be decrypted after a reinstall: the user gets a different key on the new system. Bookmarks, extensions and history do carry over. Syncing passwords and bookmarks with your Yandex account is more reliable.

firefox.notes: Passwords (logins.json and key4.db) move with the profile; if a primary password is set, you will need it on the new system. For extra safety, turn on sync with your Mozilla account.

thunderbird.notes: The profile holds your mail, address books and account settings. IMAP mail stays on the server, but local folders and POP3 mail exist only here. Saved passwords move with the profile.

dropbox.none: Dropbox: client service folders and cache

google_drive.none: Google Drive: client cache and service folders

vscode.notes: If Settings Sync is on, these settings are already in the cloud and come back when you sign in with GitHub or Microsoft. The extensions themselves are not saved: reinstall them from the extension list.

aws.config: AWS CLI settings and access keys

retroarch.notes: BIOS images in the system folder are not saved: if you need them, copy them yourself (they should be dumped from your own console). RetroArch downloads the cores again through the Online Updater.

pcsx2.user: PCSX2 memory cards, save states and settings

yuzu_ryujinx.notes: The keys (prod.keys, title.keys) are a dump from your own Nintendo Switch. They are marked as sensitive: do not share a backup that contains them. The firmware is not saved and has to be installed again.

duckstation.user: DuckStation memory cards, save states and settings

minecraft.java: Minecraft: Java Edition worlds and settings

razer_synapse.none: Razer Synapse: service folders (profiles are in the cloud)

obs.config: OBS Studio scenes, profiles and settings

spotify.none: Spotify: service folders (music and playlists are in the cloud)

telegram.notes: tdata holds the active session: a copy of this folder signs in to the account without the login code or the two-step verification password. Keep the backup in a safe place, or skip this folder and simply sign in again after reinstalling. Chats are stored in the Telegram cloud.

slack.none: Slack: service folders (messages are in the cloud)

whatsapp.none: WhatsApp: service folders (history is in the cloud and on the phone)

skype.none: Skype: service folders (history is in the cloud)

windows.start_taskbar_pins_notes: For reference only: Windows does not restore pins from a copied folder, but the saved shortcuts make it easy to pin the programs again.
